title: Conductors, Insulators and Energy
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Conductors, Insulators and Energy Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Investigate the transfer and transformation of energy in electrical circuits, including the role of circuit components, insulators and conductors (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on electrical conductors and insulators, safety, and energy changes in circuits, appliances, solar panels and wind turbines. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Insulators block it, and devices change electrical energy into light, sound, heat or movement.
body_html:
How to think about it

Conductors let electricity flow; insulators stop it.

  • Metals (copper, steel, aluminium) and graphite are conductors. Plastic, rubber, wood, glass and dry paper are insulators.
  • Wires have a copper core to carry the current and a plastic coat to keep us safe.
  • Energy is not made or destroyed in a circuit: the cell's chemical energy becomes electrical energy, then light, sound, heat or movement.
Example

Is a steel spoon a conductor?

steel is a metal

metals conduct

Answer: yes

Example

A fan motor: which energy change?

electrical energy in

movement (and some sound and heat) out

Answer: electrical to kinetic

Common mistakes

  • Thinking every shiny or hard object conducts (glass does not).
  • Thinking graphite cannot conduct because it is not a metal.
  • Saying a device makes energy (it changes energy from one form to another).

faq.q: Which materials are good electrical conductors?
faq.a: Metals such as copper, aluminium and steel are good conductors. Graphite, the 'lead' in pencils, also conducts.

faq.q: Why are electrical cords covered in plastic?
faq.a: Plastic is an insulator. It stops the current from leaving the wire, so people do not get a shock.

faq.q: What energy changes happen in a torch?
faq.a: Chemical energy in the battery changes into electrical energy, which the lamp changes into light and some heat.
